q: What is the default metric resolution (standard) in Amazon CloudWatch?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1-second resolution is available with high-resolution custom metrics.
exp.b: Incorrect. 10-second resolution is for enhanced monitoring of RDS.
exp.c: Correct. Standard metric resolution in CloudWatch is 1 minute (60 seconds). [1]
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 minutes is the basic monitoring interval for EC2 instances, not the standard resolution.

q: What is the minimum resolution available for CloudWatch high-resolution custom metrics?

exp.a: Correct. High-resolution custom metrics can have a minimum resolution of 1 second. [1]
exp.b: Incorrect. The minimum is finer than 5 seconds.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10 seconds is for RDS enhanced monitoring.
exp.d: Incorrect. 30 seconds exceeds the minimum resolution.

q: How often does EC2 basic monitoring send metrics to CloudWatch?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1-minute intervals require detailed monitoring.
exp.b: Incorrect. 3 minutes is not a standard monitoring interval.
exp.c: Correct. EC2 basic monitoring sends metrics at 5-minute intervals at no additional cost. [1]
exp.d: Incorrect. 10 minutes is longer than the basic monitoring interval.

q: How often does EC2 detailed monitoring send metrics to CloudWatch?

exp.a: Incorrect. 10-second intervals are for RDS enhanced monitoring.
exp.b: Incorrect. 30 seconds is not a monitoring interval for EC2.
exp.c: Correct. EC2 detailed monitoring sends metrics at 1-minute intervals (additional cost). [1]
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 minutes is basic monitoring.

q: How long are CloudWatch metrics with a period of less than 60 seconds retained?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 hour is too short.
exp.b: Correct. High-resolution metrics (period < 60 seconds) are available for 3 hours. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. 15 days is for 1-minute period metrics.
exp.d: Incorrect. 63 days is for 5-minute period metrics.

q: How long are CloudWatch metrics with a 1-minute period retained?

exp.a: Incorrect. 3 hours is for high-resolution metrics.
exp.b: Correct. Metrics with a 60-second (1-minute) period are retained for 15 days. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. 63 days is for 5-minute metrics.
exp.d: Incorrect. 455 days is for 1-hour metrics.

q: How long are CloudWatch metrics with a 5-minute period retained?

exp.a: Incorrect. 15 days is for 1-minute metrics.
exp.b: Correct. Metrics with a 5-minute (300-second) period are retained for 63 days. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. 455 days is for 1-hour metrics.
exp.d: Incorrect. Metrics are not retained indefinitely.

q: How long are CloudWatch metrics with a 1-hour period retained?

exp.a: Incorrect. 63 days is for 5-minute metrics.
exp.b: Incorrect. 90 days is not a standard retention period.
exp.c: Incorrect. 365 days is below the actual retention.
exp.d: Correct. Metrics with a 1-hour (3600-second) period are retained for 455 days (15 months). [1]

q: What is the default log retention period for CloudWatch Logs?

exp.a: Incorrect. 7 days is an optional setting, not the default.
exp.b: Incorrect. 14 days is not the default.
exp.c: Incorrect. 30 days is not the default.
exp.d: Correct. By default, CloudWatch Logs are stored indefinitely and never expire. You must configure a retention policy to change this. [1]

q: How many CloudWatch Alarms can you create per account per Region by default?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default is higher than 1,000.
exp.b: Correct. The default quota for CloudWatch alarms per account per Region is 5,000. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,000 exceeds the default.
exp.d: Incorrect. 50,000 is far above the default.

q: How many dimensions can a CloudWatch metric have?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 5.
exp.b: Incorrect. 10 was the old limit.
exp.c: Incorrect. 20 is below the actual limit.
exp.d: Correct. Each CloudWatch metric can have up to 30 dimensions. [1]

q: What is the maximum number of metrics per CloudWatch dashboard widget?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 100.
exp.b: Correct. A single CloudWatch dashboard widget can display up to 500 metrics. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. 1,000 exceeds the per-widget limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 2,500 is far above the limit.

q: How long does CloudTrail retain events in Event History for free?

exp.a: Incorrect. Retention is longer than 30 days.
exp.b: Incorrect. 60 days is below the actual retention.
exp.c: Correct. CloudTrail Event History retains management events for the past 90 days at no charge. [2]
exp.d: Incorrect. 365 days exceeds the free Event History retention.

q: How many trails can you create per Region in AWS CloudTrail?

exp.a: Incorrect. More trails are allowed.
exp.b: Correct. You can create up to 5 trails per Region in AWS CloudTrail. [2]
exp.c: Incorrect. 10 exceeds the default limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 20 is far above the limit.

q: How long can CloudTrail Lake retain events?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudTrail Lake retains for longer than 1 year.
exp.b: Incorrect. 3 years is below the maximum.
exp.c: Correct. CloudTrail Lake can retain events for up to 7 years (2,557 days). [2]
exp.d: Incorrect. 10 years exceeds the maximum retention.

q: How many event data stores can you create per account in CloudTrail Lake?

exp.a: Incorrect. More data stores are allowed.
exp.b: Correct. You can create up to 5 event data stores per account in CloudTrail Lake. [2]
exp.c: Incorrect. 10 exceeds the default limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 25 is far above the limit.

q: How quickly does CloudTrail typically deliver events to S3 after an API call?

exp.a: Incorrect. Delivery is not guaranteed within 1 minute.
exp.b: Incorrect. 5 minutes is faster than typical delivery.
exp.c: Correct. CloudTrail typically delivers log files within 15 minutes of an API call. [2]
exp.d: Incorrect. 1 hour is longer than the typical delivery time.

q: What is the maximum number of rules per EventBridge event bus?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 100.
exp.b: Correct. The default maximum number of rules per event bus in Amazon EventBridge is 300. [3]
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 exceeds the default limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 2,000 is far above the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of targets per EventBridge rule?

exp.a: Incorrect. More targets are allowed.
exp.b: Correct. Each EventBridge rule can have up to 5 targets. [3]
exp.c: Incorrect. 10 exceeds the maximum.
exp.d: Incorrect. 25 is far above the limit.

q: What is the maximum event size in Amazon EventBridge?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is larger than 64 KB.
exp.b: Incorrect. 128 KB is below the actual limit.
exp.c: Correct. The maximum event size in EventBridge is 256 KB. [3]
exp.d: Incorrect. 512 KB exceeds the limit.

q: How many custom event buses can you create per account per Region in EventBridge?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 10.
exp.b: Incorrect. 50 is below the actual limit.
exp.c: Correct. You can create up to 100 custom event buses per account per Region in EventBridge. [3]
exp.d: Incorrect. 300 is the rules per bus limit, not buses.

q: What is the maximum number of AWS Config rules per account per Region?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is much higher than 50.
exp.b: Incorrect. 150 was an older limit.
exp.c: Incorrect. 250 is below the current limit.
exp.d: Correct. AWS Config supports up to 400 rules per account per Region. [4]

q: How many conformance packs can you deploy per account per Region in AWS Config?

exp.a: Incorrect. More conformance packs are allowed.
exp.b: Incorrect. 25 is below the limit.
exp.c: Correct. AWS Config allows up to 50 conformance packs per account per Region. [4]
exp.d: Incorrect. 100 exceeds the limit.

q: How long does AWS Config retain configuration history by default?

exp.a: Incorrect. Default retention is longer.
exp.b: Incorrect. 90 days is CloudTrail Event History.
exp.c: Correct. AWS Config retains configuration items for 7 years by default. [4]
exp.d: Incorrect. The default is 7 years, not indefinite.

q: What is the maximum number of X-Ray sampling rules per account?

exp.a: Incorrect. More rules are allowed.
exp.b: Correct. AWS X-Ray allows up to 25 sampling rules per account. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. 50 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 100 is far above the limit.

q: What is the maximum trace document size in AWS X-Ray?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is larger.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum trace document size in X-Ray is 64 KB. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. 128 KB exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 256 KB is the EventBridge event size.

q: How long does AWS X-Ray retain trace data?

exp.a: Incorrect. Retention is longer than 7 days.
exp.b: Incorrect. 14 days is below the actual retention.
exp.c: Correct. AWS X-Ray retains trace data for 30 days. [5]
exp.d: Incorrect. 90 days exceeds the actual retention.

q: What is the default sampling rate for AWS X-Ray (first request per second)?

opts.a: 1 request per second + 1% of additional requests
opts.b: 1 request per second + 5% of additional requests
opts.c: 5 requests per second + 10% of additional requests
opts.d: 10 requests per second + 50% of additional requests

exp.a: Incorrect. The additional percentage is higher.
exp.b: Correct. The default X-Ray sampling rule traces the first request per second and 5% of additional requests. [5]
exp.c: Incorrect. The reservoir is 1, not 5.
exp.d: Incorrect. These values are too high.

q: What is the maximum number of CloudWatch Logs subscription filters per log group?

exp.a: Incorrect. More than 1 is allowed.
exp.b: Correct. Each CloudWatch Logs log group can have up to 2 subscription filters. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. 5 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 10 is far above the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of metric filters per CloudWatch Logs log group?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 10.
exp.b: Incorrect. 50 is below the actual limit.
exp.c: Correct. Each log group can have up to 100 metric filters. [1]
exp.d: Incorrect. 200 exceeds the limit.

q: Which AWS service provides a unified view of operational health across AWS resources?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudTrail records API activity, not operational health.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon CloudWatch provides monitoring and observability for AWS resources and applications, offering a unified view of operational health. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Config tracks configuration compliance.
exp.d: Incorrect. Inspector is for vulnerability assessment.

q: Which AWS service records API calls made in your AWS account?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs, not API calls specifically.
exp.b: Correct. AWS CloudTrail records API calls made in your AWS account, providing governance, compliance, and operational/risk auditing. [2]
exp.c: Incorrect. X-Ray traces application requests.
exp.d: Incorrect. EventBridge routes events between services.

q: Which AWS service helps you trace requests through distributed applications?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudTrail audits API calls, not application request flows.
exp.b: Incorrect. CloudWatch Logs stores log data but doesn't trace requests.
exp.c: Correct. AWS X-Ray helps developers analyze and debug distributed applications by tracing requests as they travel through services. [5]
exp.d: Incorrect. Config evaluates resource configurations.

q: Which AWS service continuously evaluates resource configurations for compliance?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudTrail logs API activity but doesn't evaluate compliance.
exp.b: Incorrect. CloudWatch monitors performance, not configuration compliance.
exp.c: Correct. AWS Config continuously evaluates your resource configurations against desired settings and compliance rules. [4]
exp.d: Incorrect. Trusted Advisor provides recommendations but isn't focused on continuous compliance.

q: Which service provides a serverless event bus for routing events between AWS services?

exp.a: Incorrect. SNS is a pub/sub messaging service.
exp.b: Incorrect. SQS is a message queue service.
exp.c: Correct. Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that routes events from AWS services, custom applications, and SaaS partners. [3]
exp.d: Incorrect. Step Functions orchestrates workflows.

q: What are the three states of a CloudWatch Alarm?

exp.a: Incorrect. These are not valid CloudWatch alarm states.
exp.b: Correct. CloudWatch alarms have three states: OK (metric is within threshold), ALARM (metric has breached threshold), and INSUFFICIENT_DATA (not enough data to determine state). [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. These are not the correct state names.
exp.d: Incorrect. These are not valid CloudWatch alarm states.

q: What type of CloudWatch alarm monitors a single metric?

exp.a: Incorrect. Composite alarms monitor multiple alarms, not a single metric.
exp.b: Correct. A metric alarm monitors a single CloudWatch metric or a mathematical expression based on metrics. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Anomaly detection is a feature of metric alarms, not a separate type.
exp.d: Incorrect. Multi-metric alarm is not a valid alarm type.

q: What type of CloudWatch alarm combines multiple alarms using AND/OR logic?

exp.a: Incorrect. Metric alarms watch a single metric.
exp.b: Correct. Composite alarms combine multiple alarms using Boolean logic (AND, OR, NOT) to reduce alarm noise. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Grouped alarm is not a valid type.
exp.d: Incorrect. Aggregated alarm is not a valid type.

q: What does CloudWatch Contributor Insights analyze?

opts.b: Top-N contributors to metric patterns from log data

exp.a: Incorrect. Cost optimization is not its purpose.
exp.b: Correct. CloudWatch Contributor Insights analyzes log data to create time-series visualizations showing the top-N contributors (e.g., top IP addresses, URLs, or resources). [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. IAM compliance is handled by Config/IAM Access Analyzer.
exp.d: Incorrect. While it can analyze network logs, it's broader than just network traffic.

q: What is CloudWatch Synthetics used for?

opts.b: Creating canary scripts that monitor endpoints and APIs by simulating user behavior
opts.d: Creating synthetic CloudTrail events for testing

exp.a: Incorrect. It doesn't generate test data.
exp.b: Correct. CloudWatch Synthetics creates canaries — configurable scripts that monitor endpoints and APIs by following the same routes and performing the same actions as a customer. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. It doesn't synthesize metrics.
exp.d: Incorrect. It doesn't create fake CloudTrail events.

q: What is the primary purpose of CloudWatch Anomaly Detection?

opts.b: Applying machine learning to metrics to establish baselines and detect unusual behavior

exp.a: Incorrect. Security threat detection is GuardDuty's role.
exp.b: Correct. CloudWatch Anomaly Detection uses machine learning algorithms to analyze past metric data, establish baselines, and create anomaly detection bands to identify unusual patterns. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Cost anomalies are handled by Cost Anomaly Detection.
exp.d: Incorrect. Configuration drift is AWS Config's domain.

q: What does the CloudWatch agent collect from EC2 instances that standard metrics do not include?

exp.a: Incorrect. CPU utilization is already a standard EC2 metric.
exp.b: Correct. The CloudWatch agent collects system-level metrics like memory utilization, disk space, and swap usage that are not available from standard EC2 metrics. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Network metrics are standard EC2 metrics.
exp.d: Incorrect. Status checks are standard EC2 metrics.

q: Which CloudTrail feature allows you to run SQL-based queries on events?

exp.a: Incorrect. Insights detects unusual activity, not SQL queries.
exp.b: Correct. CloudTrail Lake allows you to run SQL-based queries on your CloudTrail events for auditing and investigation. [2]
exp.c: Incorrect. Event History provides a basic view of recent events.
exp.d: Incorrect. Trails deliver events to S3 but don't support SQL queries.

q: What does AWS CloudTrail Insights detect?

opts.b: Unusual API activity and error rate spikes

exp.a: Incorrect. Compliance violations are AWS Config's domain.
exp.b: Correct. CloudTrail Insights detects unusual operational activity in your AWS account, such as spikes in API calls, resource provisioning, or error rates. [2]
exp.c: Incorrect. Application performance is CloudWatch/X-Ray's domain.
exp.d: Incorrect. Cost anomalies are handled by Cost Explorer.

q: What two types of events does CloudTrail capture?

exp.a: Incorrect. These are not the official CloudTrail event categories.
exp.b: Correct. CloudTrail captures management events (control plane operations like CreateBucket) and data events (data plane operations like GetObject, PutItem). [2]
exp.c: Incorrect. Read/write are subcategories, not the main types.
exp.d: Incorrect. These are not the official categories.

q: Is the first copy of management events free in CloudTrail?

opts.b: Yes, the first trail delivering management events to S3 is free

exp.a: Incorrect. The first trail for management events is free.
exp.b: Correct. The first copy of management events delivered to S3 via a trail is free. Additional copies and data events incur charges. [2]
exp.c: Incorrect. It's always free, not just 30 days.
exp.d: Incorrect. It's free in all regions.

q: A developer wants to monitor the memory usage of their EC2 instances in CloudWatch. The standard metrics don't show memory. What should they do?

opts.b: Install the CloudWatch agent to collect memory metrics
opts.c: Use X-Ray to trace memory usage

exp.a: Incorrect. Detailed monitoring increases frequency but doesn't add memory metrics.
exp.b: Correct. The CloudWatch agent must be installed on EC2 instances to collect OS-level metrics like memory, disk, and swap that are not available from the hypervisor. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. X-Ray is for distributed tracing, not memory monitoring.
exp.d: Incorrect. The EC2 console doesn't show memory metrics without the agent.

q: A company wants to be alerted when their EC2 CPU utilization exceeds 80% for 5 consecutive minutes. What should they configure?

opts.a: CloudWatch metric alarm with threshold > 80% and evaluation period of 5 datapoints

exp.a: Correct. A CloudWatch metric alarm monitoring CPUUtilization > 80% for 5 consecutive 1-minute datapoints (with detailed monitoring) or a specific evaluation period triggers the alert. [1]
exp.b: Incorrect. CloudTrail records API calls, not performance metrics.
exp.c: Incorrect. Config evaluates resource configurations, not performance.
exp.d: Incorrect. EventBridge scheduled rules run on a cron, not based on metrics.

q: A security team needs to know who deleted an S3 bucket yesterday. Which service should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch Logs stores application logs, not API audit trails.
exp.b: Correct. CloudTrail records all API calls including DeleteBucket, showing who made the call, when, and from where. [2]
exp.c: Incorrect. X-Ray traces application requests, not AWS API calls.
exp.d: Incorrect. EventBridge routes events but isn't the primary audit source.

q: A company wants to automatically trigger a Lambda function whenever a new EC2 instance is launched. Which service should they use?

opts.b: Amazon EventBridge with EC2 state change event pattern

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch Alarms monitor metrics, not instance state changes.
exp.b: Correct. EventBridge can capture EC2 instance state change events (e.g., 'pending' to 'running') and trigger a Lambda function target. [3]
exp.c: Incorrect. Config detects configuration changes but isn't the best for real-time triggering.
exp.d: Incorrect. Subscription filters process log data, not instance events.

q: A company wants to ensure all their S3 buckets have encryption enabled. Which service should they use?

opts.c: AWS Config with a managed rule

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch monitors performance, not configuration compliance.
exp.b: Incorrect. CloudTrail logs API calls but doesn't evaluate compliance.
exp.c: Correct. AWS Config has a managed rule (s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled) that continuously evaluates whether S3 buckets have encryption enabled. [4]
exp.d: Incorrect. X-Ray is for distributed tracing.

q: A developer's microservice is experiencing high latency. They need to identify which downstream service is the bottleneck. Which tool should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch shows individual metrics but doesn't trace request paths.
exp.b: Incorrect. CloudTrail logs API calls, not application-level request flows.
exp.c: Correct. X-Ray Service Map provides a visual representation of your application's architecture, showing latency between services and identifying bottlenecks. [5]
exp.d: Incorrect. EventBridge routes events, not trace requests.

q: A team wants to send CloudWatch Logs to both Elasticsearch and S3 simultaneously. How many subscription filters can they use per log group?

opts.a: 1 only — they must choose one destination
opts.b: 2 — they can have two subscription filters per log group

exp.a: Incorrect. More than 1 subscription filter is allowed.
exp.b: Correct. Each log group supports up to 2 subscription filters, allowing simultaneous delivery to two destinations. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. 5 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a limit of 2.

q: A company wants to reduce CloudWatch Logs costs. Their logs are retained indefinitely. What should they do first?

opts.b: Set an appropriate retention policy (e.g., 30 days, 90 days) on log groups

exp.a: Incorrect. Deleting all logs loses valuable data.
exp.b: Correct. By default, logs are stored indefinitely. Setting a retention policy (1 day to 10 years) automatically deletes older logs, significantly reducing storage costs. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Disabling logging removes observability.
exp.d: Incorrect. Moving regions doesn't address retention costs.

q: A company needs real-time notification when an IAM root user signs in. What is the best approach?

opts.b: EventBridge rule detecting AWS Console Sign-In event for root user, triggering SNS notification

exp.a: Incorrect. CPU alarms don't detect sign-in events.
exp.b: Correct. EventBridge can detect Console Sign-In events from CloudTrail and trigger an SNS notification in near real-time when the root user logs in. [3]
exp.c: Incorrect. Config tracks resource configurations, not sign-in events.
exp.d: Incorrect. X-Ray doesn't trace console sign-in events.

q: A company wants to track all changes to their Security Groups over time. Which service provides this capability?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch monitors metrics, not configuration history.
exp.b: Incorrect. CloudTrail shows who made changes but not the configuration state over time.
exp.c: Correct. AWS Config records every configuration change to resources like Security Groups, maintaining a complete timeline showing what changed, when, and who changed it. [4]
exp.d: Incorrect. EventBridge routes events but doesn't maintain configuration history.

q: What is CloudWatch Application Signals used for?

opts.b: Automatically instrument applications and track SLOs (Service Level Objectives)

exp.a: Incorrect. It's not about signal processing.
exp.b: Correct. CloudWatch Application Signals auto-instruments applications to collect metrics, traces, and logs, and enables you to set and track Service Level Objectives (SLOs). [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Push notifications are SNS's role.
exp.d: Incorrect. Network monitoring is not its primary function.

q: What is the purpose of CloudWatch Logs Insights?

opts.b: Interactively searching and analyzing log data with a purpose-built query language

exp.a: Incorrect. Predictions are not its primary purpose.
exp.b: Correct. CloudWatch Logs Insights enables you to interactively search and analyze log data using a purpose-built query language with commands like fields, filter, stats, and sort. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. It doesn't auto-fix errors.
exp.d: Incorrect. Streaming is done via subscription filters, not Logs Insights.

q: Which CloudWatch feature provides cross-account observability?

exp.a: Incorrect. Dashboards can show cross-account data but aren't the enabling feature.
exp.b: Correct. CloudWatch Cross-Account Observability enables you to monitor and troubleshoot applications spanning multiple accounts within a Region. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Alarms monitor individual metrics.
exp.d: Incorrect. Contributor Insights analyzes log patterns.

q: What are the valid destinations for CloudWatch Logs subscription filters?

opts.b: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, and AWS Lambda

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 is for log export, not real-time subscription.
exp.b: Correct. Subscription filters can deliver log events in real-time to Kinesis Data Streams, Kinesis Data Firehose, or Lambda for processing. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Lambda is one of three valid destinations.
exp.d: Incorrect. SNS and SQS are not direct subscription filter destinations.

q: What namespace does EC2 use for CloudWatch metrics?

exp.a: Incorrect. AWS/Compute is not a valid namespace.
exp.b: Correct. EC2 publishes metrics under the AWS/EC2 namespace in CloudWatch. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. The format uses 'AWS/' not 'Amazon/'.
exp.d: Incorrect. This is not the correct namespace format.

q: What does the CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) enable?

opts.b: Publishing custom metrics from Lambda and other services by embedding metric data in structured log events

exp.a: Incorrect. EMF is not about images.
exp.b: Correct. The Embedded Metric Format (EMF) allows you to embed custom metric data within structured log events, automatically extracting metrics without separate PutMetricData API calls. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. EMF doesn't embed alarms.
exp.d: Incorrect. Dashboard embedding is a separate feature.

q: What action can CloudWatch Alarms perform directly on EC2 instances?

opts.b: Stop, terminate, reboot, or recover EC2 instances

exp.a: Incorrect. Alarms can perform EC2 actions directly.
exp.b: Correct. CloudWatch Alarms can directly perform EC2 actions: stop, terminate, reboot, or recover instances without requiring Lambda or other intermediaries. [1]
exp.c: Incorrect. Auto Scaling is one action, but EC2 direct actions are also available.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda invoke is possible but not the only action.
